blockers.title: The required trustDecision has no lawful retained-event representation
evidence: v20 now says every PLATFORM-ATTESTED observation is incomplete without a retained successful trustDecision and defines one closed trustDecision shape for each supported OS/scheme pair.

The only observed attestation serialization remains exactly authenticityCore, whose closed form is {scheme, payload} with extras rejected. loaderTraces.identitySerializations.observedAttestation aliases that core and says producers emit that canonical object only.

retainedEventSchema has no trustDecision member. The closed PATHLESS laterEventVariant permits pathlessObservation and observedAttestation only; its observedAttestation again points to authenticityCore. Non-pathless retained events likewise expose taggedEvidenceForm and resolvedObjectIdentity but no platform-attestation observation envelope or trustDecision field.

A recursive key audit finds exactly two trustDecision keys in the entire artifact, both descriptive definitions under platformAttestationOperation.supportedPairs. Neither is a producer-visible retained-event field.

evidenceJoin nevertheless requires observedAttestation to be authenticityCore plus the retained trustDecision. Nesting trustDecision inside the core violates core extras rejection, while placing it beside the core has no named closed-schema location. The prose requirement and the emitted schema therefore cannot both be satisfied.
blockers.impact: No conforming producer can retain the trust result that makes a PLATFORM-ATTESTED observation complete without emitting an extra field forbidden by the closed event/core schemas. OS ABI, loader, and framework are mandatory PLATFORM-ATTESTED classes, so the required qualification evidence cannot be represented and G22 cannot yield one reproducible decision.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define one closed, producer-visible observed platform-attestation record, for example {authenticityCore, trustDecision}, with a discriminated trustDecision variant for each scheme. Name its exact location in retainedEventSchema and every applicable laterEventVariant/taggedEvidenceForm, reject extra members, and bind both members to the same pathless subject or resolvedObjectIdentity. Keep the signed authenticityCore separate and unchanged for signed-to-observed identity equality.

blockers.title: The named API labels still do not define an executable and total platform-attestation operation
evidence: For macos/codesign, the named trustDecision contains only {interfaceId, status, result}, but successResult and identifierBinding require a cdhash returned by that same successful SecCodeCheckValidity operation. No named retrieval step, output field, or association rule produces that cdhash; a standalone query is expressly excluded. The contract therefore has no executable path from the named validity result to the required payload.cdhash.

For linux/package-db, interfaceId is prose containing a two-value union, and selection is specified only as rpm-family versus dpkg-family. The same contract admits known Linux publishers including alpine and arch but maps neither those publishers nor every known publisher to one interface; an unnamed interface refuses.

The Linux operation names rpm-checksig and apt-secure without a versioned command/API, exact inputs, exit/status interpretation, returned tuple schema, or algorithm that establishes both installed-package membership and signature validity for the pathless running kernel or a file-backed owning package.

packageBytes.collection delegates the byte sequence to the database's published membership/root rule, but the contract names no such rule, version, canonical ordering, root construction, archive-versus-installed representation, or owning-package derivation. Two implementations can select different byte sequences while satisfying that prose, and a publisher with no such rule has no lawful result.

fileBackedBinding says to bind the operation to resolvedObjectIdentity, but it does not define how an object identity selects exactly one owning package or how the selected package bytes are tied to the opened object. Ambiguous ownership is mentioned only generically in failClosed.
blockers.impact: Mandatory macOS and Linux PLATFORM-ATTESTED observations do not have a single implementable identifier/trust pipeline. Implementations can diverge on the cdhash source, publisher interface, package membership, package ownership, and digest bytes, while some lawful Linux profile publishers have no named operation at all. This prevents deterministic qualification across the required platform/taxonomy matrix.
blockers.requiredRepair: For macOS, name the exact API/output operation that obtains the cdhash from the same validated SecCode object and retain the object/operation association. For Linux, provide an explicit publisher-to-interface mapping for every admitted publisher or close the admitted publisher set, name versioned executable operations and exact success/output rules, define the unique running-kernel and file-owning package lookup, and specify the canonical package byte/root algorithm in this contract. Every unsupported, ambiguous, or unavailable case must refuse before profile qualification.

shouldFix.title: retainedEventSchema still triggers the libc companion from the forbidden PLATFORM payload location
evidence: v20 correctly closes the PLATFORM-ATTESTED signed envelope as exactly {authenticityCore, optional sonameAbi}, places sonameAbi as its sibling, and keeps DIGEST-BOUND sonameAbi inside that tag's payload.
companionObservationShape and companions.SONAME-ABI.encodingByTag now use those exact per-tag locations.

The live retainedEventSchema entry still says companionObservation is required when the signed payload carries sonameAbi. A PLATFORM-ATTESTED payload is forbidden from carrying it, so that schema text makes the companion appear absent or unnecessary exactly when the lawful envelope sibling is present.
The contradiction is in normative live loader-trace schema, not a historical ledger, and it leaves producers free to retain or omit the metadata record for the same lawful signed entry.
shouldFix.impact: The authenticity envelope itself is now deterministic, but retained libc metadata is not: one conforming reading requires companionObservation from the envelope sibling and another requires it only from a payload location that PLATFORM-ATTESTED forbids. sonameAbi never changes allow/refuse, so this is a SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Replace the retainedEventSchema trigger with the same encodingByTag rule used by companionObservationShape: PLATFORM-ATTESTED envelope sibling or DIGEST-BOUND payload field. State absence only when no companion exists at that tag's one lawful location.

shouldFix.title: runIdentity plus observedAt is not guaranteed to be a unique resolver association token
evidence: v20 names the containing later-event identity (runIdentity + observedAt) as the association token and forbids cross-event composition, repairing the prior unnamed-token advisory in form.

observedAt is required only to be a monotonic non-negative integer sequence, and evidenceJoin requires each later value to be strictly greater than the one preselection value. Neither rule requires distinct later events to have distinct observedAt values or requires the value to increase strictly from one later event to the next.

Two later resolution events in the same run can therefore lawfully share runIdentity and observedAt. Swapping capturedPath from one with resolvedObjectIdentity from the other preserves the claimed token and cannot be rejected by the stated cross-event prohibition.
sequenceAndClosure is retained as a separate field, but no rule makes it part of the association token or uses it to prove observedAt uniqueness.
shouldFix.impact: The resolver record no longer relies on an impossible object-to-path projection, but its replacement token can collide and therefore cannot independently enforce same-event association. Different implementations can accept or reject the same composed evidence.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Require observedAt to be unique and strictly increasing for every event within a run, including a closed comparison rule, or include an already-unique closed event/sequence identifier in the association token. Bind capturedPath, canonicalPath, and resolvedObjectIdentity to that exact token.
